requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on the formatted type are ignored in the normal, non-surrogate path. The collector unconditionally calls CreateContractlessMembers and forces string keys, without inspecting T for MessagePackObject, Key, or IgnoreMember. Consequently, a referenced type with [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember] is serialized as a contractless map including the ignored member, contrary to the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedMessagePackFormatterRequirementTests.MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedType_AreHonoured. It generates a formatter for a referenced [MessagePackObject] type with one [Key(0)] member and one [IgnoreMember] member, then asserts an array formatter with key 0 and no serialization of the ignored member. The current contractless map implementation fails these assertions.

findings.claim: When no surrogate is specified, the collector unconditionally creates contractless string-key members and never inspects MessagePack attributes on the formatted type or its members. Consequently, a referenced type marked [MessagePackObject] with [Key] or [IgnoreMember] is serialized using a name-keyed map containing every public read-write member, rather than the declared integer keys and membership, violating the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterReferencedAttributesTests.MessagePackObjectKeysOnReferencedTypeAreHonored. It compiles a referenced assembly containing [MessagePackObject] AttributedType with [Key(0)] Value, generates an annotated formatter in a consuming compilation, and requires the formatter to use WriteArrayHeader rather than WriteMapHeader. On head it fails because the generated formatter is contractless and string-keyed.

hunches.claim: MessagePack and DataContract attributes on the formatted type are ignored: when no surrogate is supplied, generation always switches to alphabetical contractless string-key members. Consequently [Key], [IgnoreMember], [DataMember], and related annotations on T do not control the generated wire format, contrary to the requirement that attributes on T be honoured.

receipt_plan.detail:
For a referenced type [MessagePackObject] P with [Key(0)] public int A { get; set; } and [IgnoreMember] public int B { get; set; }, generate [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class PF : IMessagePackFormatter

and serialize P { A = 7, B = 9 }. Compare its bytes with those from the existing source-generated formatter for the same annotated shape. The new formatter produces a string-key map containing both A and B instead of the one-element integer-key array containing only A.

hunches.claim: MessagePack attributes already present on the formatted type are not honoured. Unless a surrogate is supplied, collection always calls CreateContractlessMembers, which assigns alphabetically ordered string-name keys and includes every public read-write member without inspecting [MessagePackObject], [Key], or [IgnoreMember]. This violates the explicit acceptance criterion for attributed external types and changes their wire contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator execution test for an external class marked [MessagePackObject], with one member marked [Key(0)] and another public read-write member marked [IgnoreMember], and a formatter using only [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]. Assert serialization produces an integer-key array containing only the keyed member. The current implementation instead produces a string-key map and includes the ignored member, so the test fails.

hunches.claim: The requirement to honour MessagePack attributes already present on T is neither implemented nor tested. When no surrogate is supplied, the collector always builds contractless members, and every external-type fixture is deliberately attribute-free, so the tests cannot detect ignored [MessagePackObject]/[Key] contracts.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type annotated with [MessagePackObject] and non-consecutive integer [Key] values plus an [IgnoreMember] property, generate its formatter without SurrogateType, and assert the array header, round-trip values, and ignored member. The current contractless implementation should emit a string-keyed map instead and fail the test.

hunches.claim: The explicit bodyless-declaration acceptance criterion has no test: all new formatter declarations use brace bodies. A regression specific to 'partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;' would therefore go unnoticed.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a generator test whose only formatter declaration is '[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] public partial class MyFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<MyType>;' and verify that generation completes without MsgPack019 or compiler errors and supplies Serialize/Deserialize.

hunches.claim: Public-field serialization in contractless mode is untested because ExternalPerson, ExternalPoint, and ExternalWidget expose only properties. The field arm of IsPublicReadWrite can stop accepting fields without failing any new test.

hunches.claim: No negative test covers duplicate surrogate keys, so removal of the uniqueness guard is not detected despite the risk of generating an invalid or ambiguous wire contract.

hunches.claim: Surrogate members without a valid integer or string [Key] are not tested. Existing negative cases all have a valid key and fail later on member matching or mixed key kinds, leaving the MemberNeedsKey guard uncovered.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Implement the formatter-generation feature together with the suggested optional SurrogateType property, using a Project-B-accessible surrogate type to supply property keys and other settings mapped to T's properties by name. Code: In addition to the core generation, the attribute exposes SurrogateType, the generator resolves and validates that type and maps its attributed properties to T by name, and the resulting metadata controls keys/settings instead of relying solely on T's own attributes or contractless defaults.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add a parameterless GeneratedMessagePackFormatter attribute whose annotated, possibly bodyless partial formatter class receives a generated implementation for T, using public-member contractless serialization by default and honoring any MessagePack attributes already present on T. Code: The generator and any associated declaration-syntax handling need only discover the marker attribute and IMessagePackFormatter<T>, emit Serialize/Deserialize members into that partial class, and inspect T across assembly boundaries; no surrogate-type property or name-based key mapping is implemented.
